title: FluidNet VLA (Vision-Language-Action) Capability Assessment

single_step_reaching.description: 2D Reaching: image shows start+target, predict 3-dim action (dx,dy,gripper)

single_step_pick_place.description: Pick-and-Place: image shows 2 objects, text specifies which to pick, predict 4-dim action

multi_step_trajectory.description: 5-step trajectory: image shows start+goal, predict 5 waypoints
multi_step_trajectory.winner: MLP (overall), but FluidNet uniquely IMPROVES over time (S5=0.125 < S1=0.687)
multi_step_trajectory.key_finding: FluidNet's ADR dynamics propagate information forward, making later predictions BETTER than earlier ones - opposite of normal models

key_findings: 1. FluidNet EXCELS at multi-object reasoning (Pick&Place winner) - ADR's local interactions are ideal for understanding object relationships
2. FluidNet shows UNIQUE temporal improvement: trajectory error DECREASES over time (S5=0.12 < S1=0.69) due to field dynamics
3. For pure spatial localization (Reaching), CNN is superior - FluidNet's Q-compression loses fine spatial detail
4. FluidNet-VLA uses 370K params vs CNN's 41K for simple tasks, but wins on complex tasks
5. The dual-stream architecture (image FluidNet + text FluidNet) effectively fuses modalities
comparison_to_transformer_vla: RT-1/RT-2 style Transformer VLA uses self-attention across image patches + text tokens + action tokens
FluidNet VLA uses ADR field dynamics instead - fundamentally different computation
Advantage: ADR naturally handles continuous spatial interactions (good for physics/contact)
Disadvantage: Cannot match Transformer's global attention for complex language understanding
Verdict: FluidNet is promising for low-level continuous control, Transformer better for high-level planning
